title: Are Large Language Models Fit For Guided Reading?
extended_summary:
This paper asks whether large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT and Bard are fit to support guided reading in children’s education. The author focuses on tasks that a reading guide or teacher would perform: generating meaningful questions from a text, producing questions that vary in cognitive difficulty, covering diverse topics within a story, and identifying portions of text a student should reread based on incorrect responses.

The study evaluates these LLMs on the FairytaleQA dataset of annotated children’s storybooks. The dataset includes storybooks for children from kindergarten through eighth grade, and the evaluation uses human annotations plus automated metrics such as ROUGE-L, BERTScore, and a diversity measure (Vendi score). The paper also compares ChatGPT and Bard against prior question-generation baselines trained specifically for FairytaleQA.

The main findings are that both LLMs can generate high-quality, semantically relevant educational questions and can recommend rereading sections of text effectively. However, their question diversity decreases as the input text grows longer, and they overproduce low-cognitive-demand questions relative to the baseline. The paper concludes that LLMs show promise as guided-reading support tools, but they need further validation before being deployed in educational settings.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's conversational large language model / chatbot used for generating and evaluating text-based outputs.
identified_tools.use_case: Evaluated as a guided-reading support tool for children’s storybooks, specifically for question-answer generation, question diversity, difficulty level of questions, and recommending text sections for rereading based on student responses.

findings.finding_summary: On the FairytaleQA validation/test set (46 storybooks), ChatGPT outperformed baseline question-generation models on BERTScore for generated questions, with reported validation/test precision 96.92/96.31, recall 95.03/96.01, and f-measure 95.96/96.15. The paper interprets this as ChatGPT generating meaningful educational questions that closely match the input text.
findings.measure: BERTScore for generated questions versus FairytaleQA reference questions

findings.finding_summary: For topic coverage/diversity, ChatGPT generated questions covering 61.4 sub-topics with one-paragraph input compared with a human diversity score of 66.8. Diversity dropped to 54.4 with two merged paragraphs and 49.4 with three merged paragraphs, indicating reduced coverage as input length increased.
findings.measure: Vendi Score-based topic diversity / sub-topic coverage

findings.finding_summary: In cognitive difficulty distribution, ChatGPT produced 3006 questions total, with 109 confirmative, 2003 explicit, and 894 implicit questions. The paper reports that 70.26% of ChatGPT's questions were low-challenge, about 20 percentage points above the baseline 53.22%, meaning ChatGPT over-generated low-challenge questions relative to human-generated baseline questions.

For text recommendation, ChatGPT achieved very high overlap with the paragraph that had been intentionally obscured through wrong answers, with BERTScore precision 98.22, recall 99.1, and f-measure 98.65. The paper concludes that ChatGPT could summarize student responses and identify the section of text a student should reread.
findings.measure: BERTScore between recommended text and target paragraph

identified_tools.name: Gemini
identified_tools.description: Google's conversational large language model / chatbot (Bard was the product name used at the time).
identified_tools.use_case: Evaluated as a guided-reading support tool for children’s storybooks, specifically for question-answer generation, question diversity, question difficulty, and recommending text sections for rereading based on student responses.

findings.finding_summary: On the FairytaleQA validation/test set (46 storybooks), Bard outperformed baseline question-generation models on BERTScore for generated questions, with reported validation/test precision 97.12/93.31, recall 95.43/96.34, and f-measure 96.27/94.80. The paper interprets this as Bard generating meaningful educational questions closely aligned to the input text.
findings.measure: BERTScore for generated questions versus FairytaleQA reference questions

findings.finding_summary: For topic coverage/diversity, Bard generated questions covering 64.2 sub-topics with one-paragraph input compared with a human diversity score of 66.8. Diversity dropped to 56.2 with two merged paragraphs and 48.2 with three merged paragraphs, indicating reduced coverage as input length increased.
findings.measure: Vendi Score-based topic diversity / sub-topic coverage

findings.finding_summary: In cognitive difficulty distribution, Bard produced 3546 questions total, with 97 confirmative, 2505 explicit, and 947 implicit questions. The paper reports that 73.38% of Bard's questions were low-challenge, about 20 percentage points above the baseline 53.22%, meaning Bard over-generated low-challenge questions relative to human-generated baseline questions.

For text recommendation, Bard achieved very high overlap with the paragraph that had been intentionally obscured through wrong answers, with BERTScore precision 97.3, recall 98.7, and f-measure 97.99. The paper concludes that Bard could summarize student responses and identify the section of text a student should reread.
findings.measure: BERTScore between recommended text and target paragraph

quality_tier_rationale: This is a single-paper evaluation of LLM outputs on proxy metrics, not a controlled study of student learning outcomes. It does not provide direct evidence that the tools improve K-12 reading/literacy relative to business-as-usual or non-AI supports.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports strong generation-quality and text-matching results, but these are task-performance proxies rather than learner outcome effects. No effect sizes on reading/literacy achievement are reported, so educational impact remains unclear.
